narrativeBlocks.title: Achilles: the burning one
narrativeBlocks.body: Achilles is glory-at-any-cost: a short life spent brilliantly, choosing fame over safety, rage and grief as the price of being the best. His model asks what excellence is worth — and what it costs everyone nearby.

narrativeBlocks.title: Odysseus: the cunning one
narrativeBlocks.body: Odysseus is endurance-through-wit: he survives by patience, disguise, and improvisation — and gets home. His model asks whether survival and cleverness are virtues or just longer-running selfishness.

narrativeBlocks.title: Theseus: the founder
narrativeBlocks.body: Theseus is the civic hero — he clears the roads not for glory but to make them safe for everyone, unites Attica, and founds the civic idea of Athens. His model is heroism as public service.

narrativeBlocks.title: Heracles: the labourer
narrativeBlocks.body: Heracles is the impossible made possible — penance, labour, and the strange fate of becoming a god after a life of pain. His model is the burden-carrier whose strength costs him everything.

narrativeBlocks.title: The question you keep answering
narrativeBlocks.body: Eight weeks of Greek heroes, and the real question was never 'which is strongest' — it's which kind of strength the world needs: the burning talent, the survivor's wit, the civic builder, or the tireless labourer. You'll meet all four again in every tradition from here.

choices.text: The burning talent who dies young
The survivor who wins by wit
The civic hero — he clears roads and founds a city rather than pursuing glory for its own sake

quiz.explanation: Theseus's heroism is public service — he clears the road for everyone else.

quiz.explanation: Heracles is the only hero whose reward is divinity itself — bought with a life of suffering.
